title: Platform systems & services: runbooks, dashboards, alerts, roadmap, and team wiki
author: Leah Park
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the Platform team's authoritative guidance for systems & services, including: an inventory of platform services, operational runbooks, how-tos for dashboards and alerts, incident playbooks and escalation paths, retrospective templates, and the 12-month roadmap. It is intended for on-call engineers, platform SREs, and new team members.

Scope

- Production and staging services owned by eng-platform (routing, auth, metrics, config, deployment pipeline, service-mesh, observability stack).
- Dashboards and alerts for service-level indicators (SLIs): availability, latency, error rate, and queue/backlog depth.
- Runbooks for sev1/sev2 events, automated mitigations, and manual recovery steps.
- Roadmap items that impact observability, reliability, and developer UX.

Systems & Services Inventory

| Service Name | Primary Owner | Purpose | Primary SLI | SLO | Runbook ID |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| ingress-proxy | platform-network | Edge routing and TLS termination | 99th latency | 99.95% availability | RB-001 |
| request-router | platform-core | Request routing to runtime clusters | 95th latency | 99.9% availability | RB-002 |
| config-store | platform-config | Central config + feature flags | read latency | 99.99% availability | RB-003 |
| metrics-ingest | observability | Metrics/metrics pipeline (Prometheus remote_write) | ingest success | 99.5% availability | RB-004 |
| alertmanager | observability | Central alert routing | delivery latency | 99.9% availability | RB-005 |
| grafana | observability | Dashboards & reporting | query latency | 99.9% availability | RB-006 |

Each runbook referenced above has an ID and lives under confluence/eng-platform/runbooks (linked at the bottom). When ownership rotates, update the 'Primary Owner' and the runbook.

Operational runbooks (template)

All platform runbooks follow this template and must be kept up to date:

1) Title and summary (1-2 lines).
2) Impact & detection (how the problem presents in dashboards/logs/alerts).
3) Immediate mitigation steps (safe short-term fixes).
4) Full recovery steps (detailed, ordered, commands).
5) Postmortem trigger conditions and next steps.
6) Pager/escalation list and contacts.
7) Related dashboards and links.
8) Last-reviewed date and reviewer.

Example: RB-002 (request-router: high request latency)

Summary: Elevated 95th percentile latency for request-router impacting hosted API tail latency. Detection: grafana dashboard "request-router / latency" shows 95th > 250ms for 5m; errors begin to surface in request-router/errors (rate > 0.5%).

Immediate mitigation (1-10 minutes)

- Verify alert (Alert rule: RouteHigh95Latency) and check last 15m on grafana.
- If autoscaler added capacity recently, confirm rollout completed: kubectl -n platform get hpa request-router.
- Scale a safe replica: kubectl -n platform scale deployment request-router --replicas=$(($(kubectl -n platform get deploy request-router -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}')+2)).
- If CPU saturating on nodes, cordon & drain a node to force scheduling to healthy nodes: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force.

Full recovery (10-120 minutes)

1. Run profiling: curl -sS http://metrics-ingest.internal/api/trace?service=request-router | jq . (internal endpoint).
2. If memory leak suspected, cycle pods with rolling restart: kubectl rollout restart deployment request-router -n platform.
3. If increased traffic from a single customer is identified, apply rate limit at ingress-proxy for that tenant: ref terraform module /modules/edge-rate-limiter (see infra repo).
4. Validate SLI recovery: 95th latency < 200ms sustained for 15m.
5. Create postmortem if outage meets severity thresholds (see "Postmortem & Retrospective" section).

Monitoring: dashboards & alerts how-to

Dashboards

- Primary dashboard owner: observability team. Secondary owners are service owners.
- Dashboard design guidelines:
  - Top-level view: current traffic, SLI graphs (P50/P90/P95/P99), errors, and downstream saturation.
  - Drill-down: per-region, per-model, per-tenant breakdowns.
  - Use time-range presets (15m, 1h, 24h) and annotate deploy times.
  - Dashboard names follow this convention: "<service> / <area>" (e.g., request-router / latency).

Grafana quick add (example)

1. Create panel -> Metrics: Prometheus -> query: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"request-router\"}[5m])) by (le))
2. Add threshold: 250ms (warning) / 500ms (critical).
3. Set alerting rule in Prometheus Alertmanager (see example alert rules).

Alerting rules (examples)

- RouteHigh95Latency (warning): 5m avg 95th latency > 250ms.
- RouteHigh95Latency (critical): 5m avg 95th latency > 500ms or error rate > 1% sustained 3m.
- MetricsIngestDown (critical): remote_write failures > 5% for 10m.

Prometheus Alert rule example (prometheus_rule.yml snippet):

```yaml
groups:
- name: platform.rules
  rules:
  - alert: RouteHigh95Latency_Warning
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\\"request-router\\"}[5m])) by (le)) > 0.25
    for: 5m
    labels:
      severity: warning
    annotations:
      summary: "request-router 95p latency > 250ms"
      runbook: "RB-002"
  - alert: RouteHigh95Latency_Critical
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\\"request-router\\"}[5m])) by (le)) > 0.5
    for: 3m
    labels:
      severity: critical
    annotations:
      summary: "request-router 95p latency > 500ms"
      runbook: "RB-002"
```

Alert routing & labels

- severity: critical | warning | info.
- team: observability | platform-core | platform-network.
- runbook: reference to runbook ID.

AlertManager config snippet (high level):

- Critical -> page on-call for platform-core then escalate to SRE lead.
- Warning -> create ticket in platform backlog, notify #platform-alerts slack channel.

Escalation path (example)

1. On-call engineer receives page (PagerDuty) and acknowledges within 5 minutes.
2. If not acknowledged in 8 minutes escalate to service owner (email & page).
3. If unresolved after 30 minutes, page SRE lead & engineering manager.
4. For critical P0 outages, initiate incident bridge and notify execs per incident communication runbook.

On-call checklist (first 10 minutes)

- Acknowledge pager and read the alert details in AlertManager.
- Open linked dashboards and logs.
- Confirm scope (single region vs global) and blast radius (all tenants or single).
- If there is a public impact, open incident post on status.redwood.com draft.
- Apply immediate mitigation from runbook.

Runbook maintenance & ownership

- Runbook owner must perform a mandatory review every 90 days. Update the "last-reviewed" field.
- When code/config changes that affect recovery steps are merged, add a note to the runbook within the release PR.
- New services must have a runbook created before owning production traffic.

Postmortem & retrospective guidance

When to write a postmortem

- P1 outage or repeated P2 within 30 days.
- SLA breach impacting customer-facing SLO.
- Any incident that required manual mitigation that isn't documented.

Postmortem template (short)

- Incident summary (what happened, when).
- Impact (affected customers, duration, SLOs breached).
- Root cause analysis (timeline of events, contributing factors).
- Immediate fixes and long-term remediation.
- Action items (owner, ETA).
- What went well / what to improve.

Example action items from recent retrospectives

- Implement per-tenant rate limiting at edge (owner: infra-team, ETA: 2026-03-15).
- Improve autoscaler metrics to include request queue depth (owner: platform-core, ETA: 2026-02-28).
- Add deploy annotations to dashboards for easier correlation (owner: observability, ETA: 2026-01-20) - DONE.

Roadmap (next 12 months)

Q1 2026 (current):
- Stabilize autoscaling policies across runtime clusters.
- Rollout per-tenant telemetry tags for SLI breakdowns.
- Migrate core dashboards to Grafana v10 panels and unified folder structure.

Q2 2026:
- Launch platform "observability catalog": managed dashboards + templated alerts (self-serve).
- Add synthetic monitoring for critical public endpoints (global latency SLO).
- Run a chaos exercise focused on ingress-proxy failover.

Q3 2026:
- Implement automatic rollback for deployments that violate error-rate SLOs.
- Introduce cost-aware alerting (token-cost anomaly detection).

Q4 2026:
- Private deployment observability parity: onboarding guides + dashboards for on-prem customers.
- Integrate KMS usage metrics into platform dashboards.

Team wiki & onboarding

- Team wiki is the single source for runbooks, on-call rotations, and tooling docs. Confluence pages should include owner, last-reviewed and links to playbooks and runbooks.
- Onboarding checklist for new platform SRE:
  1. Read this platform systems & services doc.
  2. Complete access requests: Grafana, Prometheus, PagerDuty, GitHub infra repo.
  3. Shadow on-call for one rotation (two weeks).
  4. Run through RB-001 and RB-002 runbooks in staging.
  5. Present a 15-minute runbook demo to the team.

Maintenance & governance

- Quarterly runbook audit: owners must confirm or update all runbooks.
- Alert rationalization: reduce alerts with >100 noisy incidents in last 90 days.
- Dashboard grooming: remove stale dashboards and consolidate duplicates.

Useful commands & snippets

- Check on-call schedule: pd schedule <schedule-id>
- Restart service (k8s): kubectl -n platform rollout restart deployment <service-name>
- View last deploy annotation: kubectl -n platform get deploy <service> -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.deployedAt}'
- Query 95p latency (PromQL): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"<service>\"}[5m])) by (le))

References & Related pages

Document maintenance

Owner: eng-platform on-call rotation (primary owner: Leah Park).
Last reviewed: 2026-02-10.
Review cadence: quarterly for runbooks and monthly for alerts.

If you find gaps, please file a PR against this page or ping #platform-docs in Slack.
